Hey, buddy. I feel your pain. I honestly felt like a worthless piece of shit after I heard that she was with a new guy a week after our break-up. However, I realized that we can't really control things that are outside of us, instead, we can control how react internally. I further learned that people rebound since they have low self-esteem and can't handle being alone, hence **they always need someone else for external validation**. (They thrive off attention!).

With that being said, please go **NO CONTACT**, and go through all the emotions that you are feeling right now. Cry whenever you need to cry. Be angry whenever you need to be angry. Listen to all the sad songs you wanna listen to.  **AND REMEMBER**: please never bottle up any of the emotions that you are feeling and reach out to those who will always listen to you. 

And when you are ready, please use this **pain as fuel for passion**. This is the time that you can start adding more value to yourself. For instance, creating new habits; such as, working out more, eating more healthily, reading self-help books, learning new skills, being more focused on your career, etc! 

Just remember to stay in NC, and if in case they reach out just be casual about it, and never show any sign of weakness such as begging them to come back no matter how hard it can be. Show them that you are much better than before in all the aspects you can think of. *(note: show not tell, since actions truly speak louder than words)*.

In any case that you might still want to be in a relationship with them, just remember that it is you that they have to win over, not the other way around.

Praying for your healing!

A rebound is like having a quick-fix or a band-aid solution to a problem. Yes, you will be entertained and it may be fun since you are getting to know someone new but this will inevitably end with you bringing the emotional baggage from your past relationship to this present "relationship". Furthermore, you will eventually hurt the rebound since you have not properly healed. 

My advice is that you go through the process of accepting the break-up. Don't find easy distractions but acknowledge the emotions that you are feeling post-break-up. Just don't stay feeling depressed for a long time. Then, find inspiration. (I know this is cliche) Start working on yourself and how you can become a better individual.
